title: And Now, the Curtain Call
subtitle: She brushes off the raindrops from her shoulders and steps into the new world.

trails.title: /lo/ - So which poor sap's up for the spot next?
trails.description: Pale green characters flicker incessantly, and in a second, dozens of messages appear on the fluorescent screen at the same time. It is clear to see that life must go on.

content.text: /lo/ - So which poor sap's up for the spot next?

0001 Anonymous No.92272174 ▶
Lucy has resigned. Who'll be in charge now?

0002 Anonymous No.92272271 ▶>>92272411
Ulrich? He's the second most reliable awakened in the Scientific Computing Center.

0003 Anonymous No.92272305 ▶
Someone other than Lucy, I guess.

0004 Anonymous No.92272379 ▶
No one wants that seat. It's electrified.

0005 Anonymous No.92272411 ▶>>92273050
>>92272271
Ulrich is the most opposed to this idea, he's on a hunger strike in front of the committee building. I guess he'd rather starve to death than sit in that electric chair.
How about John? He's a man with clear logic and good project management skills.

0006 Anonymous No.92272669 ▶
Lucy was an excellent leader, the casualties this time shouldn't be her fault. The best option is to let her come back.

0007 Anonymous No.92273050 ▶
>>92272411
Which John? I hope you don't mean the one who speaks in hexadecimal.

0008 Anonymous No.92273059 ▶>>92273342 >>92273451
I recommend John from the mechanical engineering group. He's very creative and forward-thinking—definitely the right person to run the Scientific Computing Center.

0009 Anonymous No.92273342 ▶
>>92273059
Last week's major power outage was caused by that John from the mechanical engineering team starting all the lab machines in parallel. He's been suspended and has been undergoing psychiatric evaluation ever since.
I'd rather pick the John from the medical team.

0010 Anonymous No.92273451 ▶>>92273773
>>92273059
John from the medical team caused a huge explosion while testing a new drug formula last month. Luckily, since he's from the medical team, help was at hand, and he's still sleeping like a baby in his hospital bed right now.

0011 Anonymous No.92273773 ▶>>92273887
>>92273451
What about John from the theoretical physics lab? His projects are absolutely safe, there's never been any danger, and there won't be any in the future. And he only cares about logic in all things—simply the perfect candidate for the man in charge.

0012 Anonymous No.92273887 ▶
>>92273773
John from the theoretical physics lab applied for a transfer a long time ago. The only person still hanging on to that group is probably Adler who forgot to transfer his files ... so Adler is indeed currently the best theoretical physicist in all of Laplace (no need to even add "one of").

0013 Anonymous No.92273982 ▶>>92274029
In the entire Scientific Computing Center, we can't find a John suitable to take charge. Isn't there a John with the judgment, execution, and long-term scientific vision of Lucy? One who will unconditionally support our research, and even be willing to approve funding for X's strange inventions or new theories on the study of ley lines? A better sense of humor than Lucy's would also be a plus.

0014 Anonymous No.92274029 ▶>>92273987
>>92273982
I think you might be able to find a John funnier than Lucy, but that's it.
My suggestion is that we all join Ulrich in preventing any politician John or placeholder John from being put in that position, and on that basis, demand Lucy's return.

0015 Anonymous No.92273987 ▶
>>92274029
Good idea, see you in front of the committee building.

0016 Anonymous No.92274024 ▶
I'll bring a few decks of cards. And can someone tell me why we're only considering Johns?

items.text: And Now, the Curtain Call
The youth are sailing for a new world.
While the old are saying goodbye to the world they knew.
Office of Director, Laplace

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Fifteen plugs. This should be enough to cover all socket types at our destination.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Simone, pass me the experiment log, please.
She brushes the dust off the desk and takes a final inventory of the lab's equipment.
She leaves the lights off, not needing them any longer.
An urgent knock sounds from the door.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Come—
Before she finishes her protocol for human social customs, the door barges open.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Madam Lucy, is it true? Are you leaving Laplace?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Yes. The inquiry is over.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: This is the decision of all parties involved.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: You have got to be kidding me!
Enigma pounds the table, sending the dust from the experiments into the air.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: After all the incredible contributions you've made, they're suspending you?!

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: This is absolutely ridiculous! Without you, there would be no umbrella, and everyone would've died from the side effects!

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Hm, but many did perish because of me. I had underestimated the danger of the ritual, and it ended up spreading uncontrollably.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Did you not once have the same opinion, Researcher Adler Hofmann?
The robot gives him a friendly nod.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: It is surprising to see you change your mind so quickly.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: But that is just what Laplace needs: the spirit of rationality and self-evolution.
The documents have been filed away.
Simone walks up to Lucy and takes the heavy experimental apparatus from her hands.
As the dust rises from their movements, Enigma lets out a cough.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I can imagine how they came to this decision. They must have considered the backgrounds of all the employees, including their social status and race.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: After eight years, we finally created an umbrella to withstand the "Storm." However, our methods for achieving such progress and breakthroughs were too much for some to handle.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: People needed an outlet for their frustrations, so someone had to be held responsible for the accidents and casualties.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Numerous complaints have been filed against me, accusing me of being a cold, heartless opponent of humanity.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Within the Foundation, Zeno, and even here, some are starting to question the idea of having an Awakened piston as the leader of Laplace.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: They argued about my arcane abilities, unsure if I had them under control or if they were becoming unstable and affecting my ability to make rational decisions.
The robot realizes an overlooked detail.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Hm. I did give the knot to Ms. Kakania in violation of the confidentiality agreement.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: But ultimately, it helped people survive, and that is all that matters.
But Enigma does not pick up on this realization.
He's already enraged, fists clenched in a ball.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: So they're questioning your standing because you're an Awakened, an arcanist?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: They're doubting the rationality of a machine that values technology and progress above all else?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Could anything be more absurd? Even I, a human, was on the verge of giving up! It was you who convinced me to save our species!

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: My question is, why are you so upset?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: This does not affect you. In fact, you may be promoted. Laplace is setting up a new department, and you and Ulrich should have been invited to head it.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Because this is damn unjust!

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: These people don't know you. They haven't worked with you or even listened to you, yet they happily reap the fruits of your labor while showing you no respect.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: The only reason you're getting suspended is because you, an Awakened, can't really die! Or they'd be honoring you with a medal on your grave right now!

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Hmm. Maybe you should take up that offer.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: At least you will get a promotion as a just reward.
Enigma opens his mouth, but no sound comes out.
He wants to tell her she's wrong about him wanting the promotion, but he's too flustered and angry to speak.
The robotic eye slit pulses, and she continues in her unemotional tone.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: By the way, Ulrich ended up receiving a medal, but like you, he was not exactly thrilled either.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: He is outside the committee building, refusing to eat in protest. But everyone knows how resilient the Awakened can be. It is going poorly.
She shakes and sighs, deeply remorseful for her subordinate's behavior.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I will suggest that one of you take this position. No one knows this research better than the two of you.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Not a chance!

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: The research must progress, and you also need to ensure that the results will not be abused.
A valid concern.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: S**t! You're right.
Enigma is caught in a fierce battle between his principles and his duty.
But the robot doesn't notice these unimportant details.
She nonchalantly walks over to the chair and runs a final battery check.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: The punishment does not bother me, Researcher Hofmann. Power exists only in your dictionary, not mine.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: From the moment of my awakening, I have been unable to comprehend you creatures. And even now, that remains unchanged.
She states, with no emotion added to embellish her delivery.
Enigma's mouth falls open in shock. Meanwhile, the robot just keeps on talking.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: We operate in different ways, just like how our fuels differ. But the bright side is, our paths align.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Whether we are creatures or machines, humans or arcanists, most of us strive for a better life. It is this primal desire that drives "progress."

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: That is why I put on the mask of a human and work on improving my appearance and speech, all for the sake of better communication with you.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Unfortunately, my efforts do not always pay off. Some say that the more human-like I appear, the more different I seem.
She shakes her head with regret.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: But I am who I am, and my motivation is not to gain recognition from others.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Our aligned path leads us to "progress," and that is all there is to it.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Thanks to the invention of the umbrella, Laplace can now resume its research unhindered. And if there is someone better qualified to lead, I am more than willing to remain a humble cog in their machine.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Besides, Ms. Z introduced me to a beautiful resort. The lake there is rich with arcane power, perfect for an Awakened arcanist like me.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Not only is it a resort, but also an independent team with a good amount of freedom. My only concern is if they have adequate power supply.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Oh, rust might be a problem. Perhaps I should ask Researcher X about his "Titanium Derust Machine."
The robot is happily thinking about her vacation plans.
She has completed all preparations for departure.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Time to go, Simone.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Madam Lucy. Please take a look at this before you go.
A stack of reports is handed in front of her.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: This is the report you compiled during the "Storm" countdown, detailing 126 side effects and how the scroll alleviates them. I have some questions about the data for Type 34.
Lucy flips it open and dutifully goes through the list one last time.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Yes. I can see a few errors in here.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Unfortunately, I have to complete all of the handover procedures today. Perhaps you can ask Mr. Ulrich about it later.
She hands it back to Enigma, but he does not reach for it.
He looks at her, grief-stricken.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: The side effects left a mark on you, didn't they?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: There are 162 side effects, not 126. There was also an obvious typo in the data for Type 34. We noticed it long ago and corrected it, took only 5 seconds.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: You sacrificed so much for this report, yet you could not see such glaring mistakes.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: You called me Researcher Hofmann earlier—a name you haven't used since you took over Laplace eight years ago. To avoid confusion with my sister, you and our colleagues started calling me Adler instead.
Moving closer, he asks grimly.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: How much data did you lose to impair your research abilities like this?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Is this why you have to leave Laplace now?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: The progress you've made has helped so many, but at what cost to your own well-being!
The robot does not answer, a rare occurrence.
From her side, Simone gently takes the file for her.

items.speaker: Assistant Simone
items.text: We should go, Madam Lucy.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Hm. Goodbye, Researcher Adler.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Thank you for correcting my mistake.
She walks away with steely steps, not looking back.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Alright, fine!
He grips the doorframe, ignoring the strange looks from the hallway.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I'll take up that role and do what you've been nagging me to do. I'll take care of those pesky committees.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: But just so you know, I'm not doing this for the higher-ups who look down on us,

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: but for the people who look up to us from below!
The footsteps continue in rhythm.
Her duty here is done.
Then, another voice calls out.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: Madam Lucy!

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Hm?
The corridors are bustling with people.
Researchers, clerks, directors, and security ...
Every Laplace employee is in the corridors, from bottom to top floor.
The same voice shouts.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: All attention!

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: Salute!
Papers litter the air like snowflakes.
Everyone says goodbye in their own language, tossing files over the railings.
The countless drafts, designs, and forms from the past 24 hours rain down.
They were created for the "Storm," and have completed their mission.
Just as did the robot.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Simone, why are they throwing papers at me? Are they rejecting me and banishing me?

items.speaker: Assistant Simone
items.text: On the contrary, madam, they are showing their reverence.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Oh, I see.
The robot is without a face and emotion module today, so she turns away from the crowd.
The sunlight dances on her metallic surface, enveloping her in a golden aura.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Let us go, Simone.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I miss the Laplace chargers already.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: There is a 230-volt bath at the resort, right?
THE END
